page: Amazon Web Services t3a.xlarge is a burstable performance instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at 2.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, and 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the t3a.xlarge operates primarily in the lower performance tiers. In stress-ng CPU testing, both single-core and multi-core performance fall within the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only small block cached bandwidth scoring in the bottom 25% and large block write bandwidth in the bottom 10%. However, the processor demonstrates moderate capability in cryptographic tasks, achieving an average rating in the PassMark CPU encryption test. Other workloads, such as static web serving, software compilation, and Redis SET operations, fall into the weak to poor performance categories.

The burstable CPU allocation model of the t3a.xlarge offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads with variable CPU utilization, allowing users to access resource density without paying for continuous high-compute capacity. The primary tradeoff is the performance ceiling; sustained heavy workloads will deplete CPU credits and face throttling. Consequently, this instance is best suited for low-traffic web servers, development environments, small databases with intermittent query patterns, and basic background worker tasks that do not require continuous high-throughput compute or memory performance.
description: Amazon Web Services t3a.xlarge is a burstable general-purpose instance utilizing the Nitro hypervisor and an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7571 processor. It features 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps, with no local storage or GPU. Designed for workloads with variable CPU utilization, its burstable allocation model offers qualitative cost efficiency for intermittent tasks. However, benchmark results show performance constraints, with CPU and memory bandwidth tests largely scoring in the bottom 10% to 25%, though cryptographic encryption performance remains average. This instance is best suited for non-production environments, low-traffic web serving, and light database operations.
